title: Smooth transporters between multiplicative-type subgroups
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $G\to S$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine group scheme of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; affine means that $G=\operatorname{Spec}C$ for an $A$-algebra $C$. Group schemes have multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams [def-sc-group-scheme] over $S$. Let $H,H'\hookrightarrow G$ be closed subgroup schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] of multiplicative type: fppf locally on $S$, each is isomorphic to a diagonalizable group $D_R(M)=\operatorname{Spec}R[M]$ [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group] over an affine base $\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $M$ a finitely generated abelian group. The character group may vary on the covering, and the groups may be nonreduced. Fppf coverings are faithfully flat finitely presented coverings [def-pc-fppf-site]. Define a functor on $S$-schemes by
$$Z(V)=\{g\in G(V):gH_Vg^{-1}\subseteq H'_V\},$$
where containment means containment of subgroup functors after every $V$-scheme extension. Then $Z$ is represented by a closed subscheme of $G$ of finite presentation over $S$, and $Z\to S$ is smooth. The representing subscheme and its inclusion into $G$ commute with arbitrary base change $S'\to S$. No conjugacy, equal-rank, or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed, and $Z$ is allowed to be empty.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 2.1.2, printed p.56, and proof pp.57--59, restricted to a Noetherian affine base and to both subgroups of multiplicative type. The transporter is the containment functor defined at the start of Section 2.1. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this assertion.

proof.text: Choose fppf covers splitting $H$ and $H'$. Base change one cover along the other and compose them; these are again fppf coverings by the base-change covering lemma and the transitivity axiom of a site in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Use the affine refinement lemma to obtain finitely many affine $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ covering $S$ on which both groups split, with character groups $M_i,N_i$. Put $U=\coprod_iU_i$. The coproduct-cover encoding makes $U\to S$ a singleton fpqc cover. Over each $U_i$, write $G_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$; the affine fibre-product formula gives $C_i=R_i\otimes_A C$. The closed-immersion affine criterion identifies $H'_i$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i/I_i)$ for an ideal $I_i$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $R_i$ will be needed for the local construction.

source.place: Tag 021L (fppf pretopology); affine refinement; Conrad Proposition 2.1.2, local construction, printed pp.57--59.

proof.text: Fix $i$, abbreviate $R_i,C_i,M_i,I_i$ to $R,C,M,I$, and use $H_i=D_R(M)$. Conjugation $q:G_i\times_RH_i\to G_i$, $(g,h)\mapsto ghg^{-1}$, gives $q^*:C\to C\otimes_RR[M]$. Uniquely expand $q^*(f)=\sum_m a_{f,m}\otimes e_m$ for every $f\in I$, each sum having finite support. Let $J\subseteq C$ be generated by all $a_{f,m}$ and put $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)$, a closed subscheme by the quotient-spectrum lemma. For an $R$-algebra $B$, a point $g:C\to B$ lies in $Z_i(B)$ exactly when $\sum_m g(a_{f,m})e_m=0$ in $B[M]$ for every $f\in I$. This says precisely that $H_B\to G_B$, $h\mapsto ghg^{-1}$, factors through $H'_B$. It is equivalent to the required containment after every $B$-algebra extension: necessity follows by testing the universal $H$-point over $B[M]$, and sufficiency follows by evaluating that universal point. Coefficient uniqueness uses the free group-algebra basis, even with torsion in $M$ and nilpotents in $B$. The same calculation with coefficients mapped to any base algebra proves base-change compatibility of this closed subscheme. Morphism gluing on affine opens of an arbitrary test scheme extends the representation from affine tests to all tests.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2, representability, printed pp.58--60; agent coefficient version of the universal closed conditions, without torsion-level intersections.

proof.text: Form $G_U=\coprod_iG_i$ and $Z_U=\coprod_iZ_i$. On each overlap $U_i\times_SU_j$, the two pullbacks represent exactly the same containment subfunctor of $G$, by step 2. Yoneda gives a unique isomorphism over the ambient group, and uniqueness gives its cocycle. The coproduct descent encoding packages these as a singleton datum for $Z_U\to G_U$ relative to $G_U\to G$. This is an fpqc cover, by base change of $U\to S$. Each $Z_i\to G_i$ is affine, being a quotient-spectrum immersion, so $Z_U\to G_U$ is affine by the affine-cover criterion on the disjoint components. Effective affine descent gives $Z\to G$. Closed-immersion descent makes it a closed immersion. This $Z$ represents the desired functor: a morphism $V\to G$ factors through $Z$ iff its pullbacks to the fpqc cover $V\times_SU$ factor through $Z_U$. Indeed, the local factorizations agree on overlaps because the inclusions are monomorphisms, and representable fpqc descent glues them uniquely. The identical argument with the closed immersion $H'\to G$ shows that containment itself can be tested on this cover. Thus the local representation is the global one, including for non-affine $V$.

source.place: Tags 0245 (lemma-affine), 02L6 (lemma-descending-property-closed-immersion), 0241 (lemma-fully-faithful); uniqueness of representing objects, Categories Tag 001P.

proof.text: Since $G=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is affine and $Z\to G$ is closed, the affine-cover criterion gives $Z=\operatorname{Spec}Q$ with $C\twoheadrightarrow Q$. The ring $C$ is of finite type over $A$ by hypothesis, so its quotient $Q$ is of finite type: images of any finite algebra-generating set of $C$ generate $Q$. As $A$ is Noetherian, the finite-type/finite-presentation lemma makes $Q$ finitely presented over $A$. Its finite polynomial presentation is precisely a finite presentation of the affine morphism $Z\to S$. The same lemma also makes $C$ finitely presented over $A$. Tensoring these finite presentations with any $A$-algebra gives finite presentations of every affine base change of $G$ and $Z$.

Work over a splitting affine $\operatorname{Spec}R=U_i$. Take any commutative $R$-algebra $B$, an ideal $K$ with $K^2=0$, and $g_0\in Z_i(B_0)$, where $B_0=B/K$. Its conjugation on $H_{B_0}$ factors uniquely through $H'_{B_0}$ as a group homomorphism $v_0:D_{B_0}(M_i)\to D_{B_0}(N_i)$. The group diagrams hold after the inclusion into $G$, hence before it since that inclusion is monic. Character duality describes $v_0$, locally on $\operatorname{Spec}B_0$, by character maps $\alpha:N_i\to M_i$. Since $N_i$ is finitely generated, finitely many generators give finitely many group-algebra coefficients, so the locally constant character map takes finitely many values. Its fibres form a finite clopen partition. The clopen-idempotent correspondence and lifting idempotents through $K$ lift this partition to $\operatorname{Spec}B$: products of distinct lifted idempotents are the unique lift of zero and hence zero; their sum is the unique lift of one. On each piece use the monomial homomorphism $e_n\mapsto e_{\alpha(n)}$. Glue these maps to a homomorphism $v:H_B\to H'_B$ reducing to $v_0$. For $B=0$ this is the unique map between empty schemes; otherwise $B_0\ne0$, so the nonzero-ring hypothesis of character duality holds on every nonempty piece.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2 smoothness paragraph, printed pp.57--58, with Appendix B.1, printed pp.280--281; Stacks Tags 00EE and 00J9 for lifting the finite character partition.

proof.text: Smoothness of $G$ supplies a lift $g\in G(B)$ of $g_0$. Compare $f_1=\operatorname{Int}(g)\circ j_B:H_B\to G_B$ with $f_2=j'_B\circ v:H_B\to G_B$. They have exactly the same reduction, not merely the same image. The group $G_B$ is affine and finitely presented by step 4. It is smooth: for a lifting problem over $B$, forget to the lifting problem for $G/S$, take its lift, and pair that lift with the prescribed map to $\operatorname{Spec}B$; local finite presentation follows from the tensor presentation. Apply split-diagonalizable infinitesimal conjugacy to $f_1,f_2$. It gives $u\in G(B)$ reducing to $1$ with $\operatorname{Int}(u)f_1=f_2$. Therefore $\operatorname{Int}(ug)j_B=j'_Bv$, so $ug\in Z_i(B)$ and its reduction is $g_0$. This solves every affine square-zero lifting problem for $Z_i$. Step 4 gives its finite presentation; the definition of smoothness now proves $Z_i\to U_i$ smooth. Neither injectivity nor smoothness of $H_i,H'_i$ was used in the conjugacy theorem.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2 smoothness paragraph, printed pp.57--58; Corollary B.2.6 and Remark B.2.4, printed pp.285--287; use homomorphisms with identical reductions to avoid a separate subgroup-identification lemma.

proof.text: The map $U\to S$ is flat and surjective since the $U_i\to S$ form an fppf cover. It is quasi-compact: every $U_i$ is affine and hence quasi-compact, a finite union of quasi-compact components is quasi-compact, and $S$ is affine and hence quasi-separated, so the qcqs permanence lemma applies. Smoothness of $Z_U\to U$ is the componentwise conclusion of step 6 (local finite presentation is checked on the components; for an affine square-zero test, its inverse images of the finitely many clopen components lift uniquely by idempotent lifting, and the lifts supplied by step 6 on those pieces glue). Smooth fpqc base descent therefore proves $Z\to S$ smooth.

source.place: Tag 02VL, lemma-descending-property-smooth, finite affine splitting cover.

proof.text: For an arbitrary $S'\to S$ and an $S'$-scheme $V$, maps $V\to Z\times_SS'$ over $S'$ are exactly maps $V\to Z$ over $S$. The latter, by step 3, are those $g\in G(V)=G_{S'}(V)$ satisfying $gH_Vg^{-1}\subseteq H'_V$ after every $V$-scheme extension. These are precisely the points of the transporter formed from $H_{S'},H'_{S'}$ in $G_{S'}$. This natural identity proves that $Z\times_SS'$ represents that transporter, even if $S'$ is not Noetherian or the base change is not flat. Yoneda identifies the comparison uniquely; both inclusions into $G_{S'}$ send a point to that same $g$, so the inclusions agree. Uniqueness gives compatibility with composition of base changes. If the coefficient ideal is the unit ideal the same construction gives the empty scheme, and the lifting assertions are vacuous wherever no residual point exists.

Step 4 is 00FP. In step 6 the reductions of f1 and f2 are equal and G_B is smooth and finitely presented, and the left correction ug is right. In step 7, U->S is flat, quasi-compact and surjective, and Z x_S U = Z_U. Step 8 is formal. Duplicate search over the 15 transporter hits found no equal statement.
